footer.disclaimer: Not a medical device. It does not replace the alarms of your CGM, insulin pump or medical app.

caution.title: Not a medical device. Not a replacement for real alarms.
caution.text: Blood Glucose Monitor only adds extra hints to Home Assistant. It does not replace the alarms of your CGM, insulin pump or medical app (for example Dexcom, LibreLink, CamAPS FX or xDrip+). Keep those alarms switched on at all times. Notifications from Home Assistant can be delayed or not arrive at all, for example when Home Assistant, your network or the glucose data source is down. Never rely on them alone. Use at your own risk; there is no warranty of any kind.

home.title: Information
home.description: Extra glucose hints for Home Assistant: alarms, reminders and reports as building blocks for your own notifications. Not a medical device.
home.headline: Extra glucose hints for Home Assistant
home.lead: Blood Glucose Monitor turns the glucose data of another integration (for example Nightscout or Dexcom) into optional alarms, reminders and reports, one entry per person. The integration decides when; you decide how you are notified.

cards.title: Glucose alarms
cards.text: Urgent low, low, high, urgent high, falling fast, rising fast and data loss, each with delay, repeat, acknowledge, snooze and re-check. Urgent low is never paused.

cards.title: Reminders
cards.text: Charging reminder for the phone in the evening, and change reminders for cannula, CGM sensor and insulin reservoir with an optional warning before they are due.

cards.title: Reports
cards.text: A summary per period of a schedule (for example night or school): minimum, maximum, mean, time in range and the alarms of the period.

cards.title: Your notifications
cards.text: Every alarm and the report has an event entity. Your own automations decide how to notify: phone, speaker, light. The automation builder prepares them.

home.shot_notifications: Notifications from an automation of the builder, with the ready-made texts of the integration (here as Home Assistant notifications).
home.secondary_text: The integration is meant as a second line: extra information for the household, a hint on the speaker at night, a reminder that the phone needs charging. It depends on Home Assistant, the network, the glucose integration and the phone, and any of these can fail without warning. The primary alarms belong to the CGM, the pump or the medical app.
secondary_points: Without a reading time of the glucose data there are no glucose alarms; a repair issue tells you so. Nothing is guessed.
Stale data neither starts nor ends a glucose alarm; the data loss alarm covers missing data.
Alarm states survive a restart of Home Assistant.
start_steps: Install Blood Glucose Monitor from the Marketplace: add EarMaster/home-assistant-blood-glucose-monitor as a custom repository of type Integration, download it and restart Home Assistant.
Add the integration under Settings → Devices & services, once per person: confirm the notice, enter the name and select the glucose sensor and, optionally, the person.
Under Configure, switch on what you need: thresholds for the alarms, the charging and change reminders, the report periods.
Create the notifications: open the automation builder from the device page of the person (Visit) or from the Configure menu. It already knows the entities of that person.

entities: The most important current state, with the latest glucose value, trend and active alarms as attributes.
Trigger for notifications. One per alarm; fires on start, repeat, acknowledge and end, and before a change is due (optional warning).
State of the alarm (idle, pending, active, snoozed) for dashboards and conditions. It does not change on a repeat.
Acknowledges the alarm for its snooze time.
Silences all alarms except urgent low for the configured time.
Due time of a change reminder and recording a change.
The report of each period; the sensor holds the time in range of the last one.

home.about_text: I develop Blood Glucose Monitor for myself and my family, and I hope it is helpful for others too. If you would like to support my work, you can do so on Liberapay or Buy Me a Coffee.
home.contribute_text: Blood Glucose Monitor is an open project, and contributions are welcome:
contribute_points: Ideas and feature requests: what would help you in everyday life with diabetes?
Bug reports: something does not work as described? Please describe what you expected and what happened.
Translations: improvements to the existing languages or a new language for the integration and this site.
home.contribute_link: Open an issue on GitHub or send a pull request.
home.my_ha_alt: Open your Home Assistant instance and open this repository in the Marketplace.

builder.title: Automation builder
builder.description: Prepare a notification automation for the events of Blood Glucose Monitor.
builder.lead: Pick the events and the phone; the builder prepares one automation that sends a notification with the ready-made text of the integration. Adjust it in Home Assistant if you want more.
builder.caution_text: These notifications can be delayed or missing. Keep the alarms of your CGM, insulin pump or medical app switched on.
builder.prefill_note: Prefilled from Home Assistant: only the events that are set up for this person are shown, with their entity IDs.
builder.manual_note: Tip: open the builder from Home Assistant (device page of the person → Visit, or Configure of the entry) to get the right entity IDs. Here they are guessed from the name; check them under Settings → Devices & services → Entities.
builder.notify_hint: The notify action of the phone, for example notify.mobile_app_pixel_8 (see Developer tools → Actions). Several, separated by commas.
builder.events_hint: Started or repeated → notification. Acknowledged or over → the notification is removed again.
builder.paste_hint: In Home Assistant: Settings → Automations & scenes → Create automation → Create new automation, then ⋮ → Edit in YAML, paste and save.
builder.shot_automation_alt: Automation editor with the trigger Event received on the low alarm and the report

docs.title: Documentation
docs.description: Event entities, event types, requirements and attributes of Blood Glucose Monitor.
docs.lead: Which events there are, when they fire and which values they bring along. For setup and options see the README on GitHub.
docs.events_text: Every active alarm and reminder has its own event entity next to its state sensor and its acknowledge button, for example Low alarm. The report has the event entity Report. Automations use the trigger Event received with one or more event types:
types: the alarm starts and on every repeat
the alarm is acknowledged or over
the warning of a change reminder
docs.values_text: The event types are unique per person, so an automation can target the entity or the whole device of the person. The values of an event are the attributes of the entity, in templates trigger.to_state.attributes.<name>; the event type is trigger.to_state.attributes.event_type.
docs.shot_automation_alt: Automation editor with the trigger Event received
docs.shot_automation: The trigger Event received in the automation editor.
docs.sensors_text: The state sensors of the alarms are for dashboards and conditions; they do not change on a repeat, so they are not suited as triggers.
docs.alarm_values_text: All alarm and reminder events have these attributes; values that do not apply are empty.
ack_points: Acknowledge silences an alarm for its snooze time; then it is checked again and starts at once if it still applies. Ways: the Acknowledge … button, the action blood_glucose_monitor.acknowledge or a notification action with the id from ack_action.
Pause alarms silences all alarms except urgent low for the configured duration and turns off by itself.
Record a change of cannula, sensor or reservoir with the … changed button or the action blood_glucose_monitor.record_change (optionally with a time in the past).

js.entity_note: Entity {entity}; the entity ID depends on the language of Home Assistant when the entry was set up.
js.automation_description: Created with the Blood Glucose Monitor automation builder.

req.threshold_set: A threshold entity is selected in {menu}.
req.below_for_delay: The glucose stays below the threshold for the delay.
req.above_for_delay: The glucose stays above the threshold for the delay.
req.reading_time: The glucose data has a reading time (a reading time sensor or the date attribute of the glucose sensor). Without it there are no glucose alarms and a repair issue tells you so.
req.reading_time_short: The glucose data has a reading time (a reading time sensor or the date attribute of the glucose sensor).
req.fresh: The latest reading is not older than the maximum data age of the data loss alarm; stale data neither starts nor ends a glucose alarm.
req.home: With Only when the person is at home in {menu}: the person is at home when the alarm would start. A running alarm continues when the person leaves.
req.not_acknowledged: The alarm is not acknowledged: after an acknowledgement it stays silent for the snooze time and is then checked again.
req.pause_never: The pause does not apply to this alarm.
req.repeats: Repeats: the event fires again in the repeat interval while the alarm is active (repeat interval 0 = only once).
req.acknowledged: The alarm is acknowledged: the Acknowledge … button, the action blood_glucose_monitor.acknowledge or the notification action ack_action.
req.back_above: The glucose reaches the threshold plus the clear offset.
req.back_below: The glucose falls to the threshold minus the clear offset.
req.detection_set: A detection is selected in {menu}: trend or own rate of change.
req.fall_trend: Trend: the trend of the glucose data (trend sensor or direction attribute) falls quickly (or only very quickly, as set).
req.fall_rate: Own rate: two readings at most 15 minutes apart fall faster than the rate limit per minute.
req.fall_delay: The fast fall lasts for the delay.
req.fall_over: The glucose no longer falls fast.
req.rise_trend: Trend: the trend of the glucose data (trend sensor or direction attribute) rises quickly (or only very quickly, as set).
req.rise_rate: Own rate: two readings at most 15 minutes apart rise faster than the rate limit per minute.
req.rise_delay: The fast rise lasts for the delay.
req.rise_over: The glucose no longer rises fast.
req.no_reading: No new reading arrives within the maximum data age.
req.charging_set: A battery level and a charging state sensor are selected in {menu}.
req.charging_time: It is between the reminder time and midnight.
req.charging_state: The phone is not charging and the battery is at or below the limit.
req.charging_over: The phone charges. After midnight a running reminder waits for charging; no new one starts before the next reminder time.
req.change_duration: A wear duration (field or entity) is set in {menu}.
req.change_last: The last change is known: from the selected last change entity, or recorded with the … changed button or the action blood_glucose_monitor.record_change.
req.change_due: The due time is reached: last change plus wear duration, or the fixed time on the due day.
req.change_next: The next change is recorded (button, action or a new time of the last change entity).
req.soon_set: A warning time (Warning before) is set in {menu}.
req.soon_once: It fires once per due time, this long before the due time.
req.soon_away: While the person is away (with Only when the person is at home) or alarms are paused, it is sent as soon as possible before the due time.
req.report_entity: An entity with the periods (for example a schedule helper) is selected in {menu}.
req.report_end: A period ends: the entity turns off. A period that ends during a restart is reported afterwards.
req.report_home: With Only when the person is at home in {menu}: the person is at home when the period ends. The Last report sensor is updated anyway.
req.report_stats: Statistics need the recorder; the time in range needs a low (or urgent low) and a high (or urgent high) threshold.

attributes.title: Ready-made title in the language of Home Assistant, for example Alex: low glucose.
attributes.message: Ready-made message: glucose with unit and trend arrow for the glucose alarms, a matching text for data loss and the reminders; on acknowledge or end a short text.
attributes.alarm: Key of the alarm, for example low.
attributes.glucose: Latest glucose value in the unit of the glucose sensor.
attributes.rate: Own rate of change per minute.
attributes.data_age_min: Age of the latest reading in minutes.
attributes.entry_id: ID of the config entry, for the actions of the integration.
attributes.tag: Notification tag, unique per person and alarm. Use it to replace and clear the notification.
attributes.ack_action: Mobile app notification action that acknowledges this alarm.
attributes.battery: Battery level of the phone in percent.

report_attributes.title: Ready-made title, for example Alex: report.
report_attributes.duration_min: Length of the period in minutes.
report_attributes.below: Share of the time below range in percent (empty without both thresholds).
report_attributes.in_range: Share of the time in range in percent (empty without both thresholds).
report_attributes.above: Share of the time above range in percent (empty without both thresholds).
report_attributes.coverage: Share of the period with glucose data in percent.
report_attributes.alarms: Number of alarms that started in the period, per alarm.
report_attributes.low_alarms: Number of low and urgent low alarms in the period.
report_attributes.tag: Notification tag, unique per person, so a new report replaces the last one.
